newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico blue chips at new record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico blue chips at new record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended mixed on Wednesday, although blue chips ended with a toehold in record territory on Wednesday after what analysts and dealers said was a very selective recovery.
"We saw gradual profit-taking through the day, but also buying that absorbed it," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy. Final closing prices placed
the blue chip IPC index ended up 4.69 points, or 0.11 percent, at a record 4,281.52. The broad market balance, however, was negative. Out of 108 stocks traded, sliders outpaced gainers by 45 to 42.
Galvan said the broad market trend was due to light profit-taking rather than a sell-off, as overall volume was lackluster.
"This shows a trend among investors to hold positions," he added.
Trading volume was slower than many recent sessions at 95.96 million shares.

"Stocks recovered on delayed buying by small investors, who always step into a rally after the big players have bought," another analyst said. "The unemployment data were good, but did not explain the recovery."
"Lower inflation has halted the slide in purchasing power, but we still await a recovery in real income to boost consumption," the analyst sadded.

The National Statistics Institute announced during morning dealing that open unemployment in Mexico fell to 3.9 percent in May, from 4.29 percent in April. A Reuters survey of 13 financial houses had previously predicted an average rate of 4.12 percent.
Dealers said, however, that strong industrial output data released Tuesday helped the blue chip recovery. A breakdown showed manufacturing and construction drove the increase.

Financial group Bancomer A shares were the most heavily traded gainer of the day, up 8 centavos to 2.18 pesos. Nonetheless, dealers said the stock gained on switching with its B shares, which meanwhile fell 11 centavos to 3.82 percent after recent sharp gains.
Bancomer's two share series, which are both included in the IPC, accounted for 23 percent of all shares traded.
Telecomms stock Telmex weighed heavily on the market, and ended down 18 centavos at 18.52 pesos, while its ADRs 3/8 at 46-3/4.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile slumped 42.07 points to 7,718.71.
"Cemex was one of the few interesting stocks today, although Alfa and GCC also did well," a floor trader said.

Cement maker Cemex CPO shares gained 55 centavos to 32.25 pesos, while its B shares were up 65 centavos to 35.50 pesos, and its A shares rose 65 centavos to 32.35 pesos. All three share series are included in the IPC.
Cement stock Grupo Cementos de Chihuahua (GCC) ended up 10 centavos at 8.70 pesos. Conglomerate Alfa meanwhile gained 60 centavos to 51.60 pesos.
